subject: BrightHealth evaluation cadence — containment options and escalation
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: BrightHealth evaluation — schedule pressure and containment options

Team / Jared,

Quick note — during today's check-in Jared called out procurement gating a couple of acceptance criteria and sign-off items. That threatens our agreed evaluation close (target: 2027-06-11) because two items require a procurement PO and legal review (data retention appendix + customer hosting plan).

I've attached a tight risk log and the latest MAP slice (BrightHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx) showing which tasks are blocking the close. High level:
- Procurement hold on PO issuance (expected delay: 2-3 weeks)
- Legal redline on data retention appendix (Jared/pri says minor, but needs review)
- Integration test window needs +5 days to satisfy BrightHealth acceptance tests

Options I see now (short, operational asks):
1) Re-baseline: push close by 2–3 weeks; preserve go/no-go criteria but shift dates
2) Containment: provide a scoped acceptance short-list (make final delivery conditional on non-blocking items) and offer a limited service credit if we need an extended evaluation window
3) Escalate: get exec sign-off for a temporary credit and procurement prioritization from BrightHealth

Jared — can you confirm procurement ETA and whether BrightHealth can accept a scoped acceptance path?
Marissa / Grace — tagging you for risk acceptance and help drafting an exec note if we need to offer a credit.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightHealth_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP snapshot), BrightHealth_risk_log.csv (staged)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: BrightHealth evaluation — schedule pressure and containment options

Aditya / Jared — thanks, quick update from my side after reviewing the MAP and talking to the delivery team. I pulled a focused risk log and proposed containment plan (see attached). Key points: 

- Procurement: PO paperwork is the blocker. If BrightHealth can commit to a PO submission date within 10 business days, we can preserve the current go-live gating that depends on the PO for licensing + support. If not, we should re-baseline.
- Legal/data retention: draft redline is small (3 lines) — we can accept a provisional appendix for evaluation (signed acknowledgement) and continue detailed legal review in parallel.
- Acceptance tests: delivery can run a compressed validation window (reduce parallel test runs) that wastes less customer time but requires an extra integration engineer day.

Proposed containment (operational):
- Path A (fast): BrightHealth signs provisional data appendix + commits to PO submission within 10 business days. We keep the 11 Jun close target; delivery adds 5 days of validation inside the existing window and we provide a 10% evaluation credit if the PO slips past 10 business days.
- Path B (re-baseline): Move close to 2027-06-29, allow procurement and legal to finish, no credit required.

I added items to the risk log (BrightHealth_risk_log.csv) with owners and ETA columns. Action items:
- Jared: confirm PO submission date and whether BrightHealth can sign a provisional appendix by EOD tomorrow.
- Aditya: if Jared can't meet Path A timelines, prepare an exec note for Grace to approve a short extension + credit.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: BrightHealth_risk_log.csv, containment_plan_v1.docx

> On Mon, May 24, 2027 at 09:12 Aditya Rao wrote:
> > Team / Jared,
> > ...
From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@brighthealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: BrightHealth evaluation — schedule pressure and containment options

Thanks Aditya/Marissa — quick clarity from our side. 

Procurement: our procurement office needs internal budget approval before issuing the PO. The earliest credible date I can give today is 2027-06-07; I can push to get provisional approval by 2027-05-31 but cannot promise. Legal: the data retention appendix looks straightforward and our counsel is okay with a provisional sign if Redwood agrees to follow-up confirmation.

We prefer Path A (keep close date) but only if Redwood can accept a provisional appendix and provide a scope-limited acceptance path. The evaluation team is time-boxed and we cannot extend indefinitely. If Redwood requires legal final sign-off before close, we will have to re-baseline.

I will escalate procurement internally and let you know the 5/31 provisional promise by EOD tomorrow.

—Jared
Jared Lowe
Director, Vendor Procurement | BrightHealth
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@brighthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: BrightHealth MAP pressure — request for short extension + credit approval (if needed)

Grace / Marissa — per Jared's note, procurement may not commit until 06/07. That pushes us close to the edge for the 06/11 close. If we want to keep the customer in the current evaluation window, I recommend we pre-authorize Path A: accept the provisional data appendix, and approve a conditional evaluation credit if the PO comes after 10 business days from today (5/24). Proposed terms:

- Re-baseline threshold: if PO submission > 10 business days from 2027-05-24 (i.e., after 2027-06-07), Redwood offers a 10% evaluation credit applied to first month of paid usage (non-refundable credit, limited to evaluation period).
- Timebox: provisional appendix signed now; final legal signature within 30 days after PO.
- Internal constraint: Product/delivery will run compressed validation; we will not escalate engineering priority beyond the agreed trial scope unless commercial is approved.

If you approve, I'll (a) update the MAP and risk log, (b) send an official acceptance path to BrightHealth, and (c) notify Legal & Finance to prepare the credit note.

Aditya
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: procurement_ask.docx (credit template)

> On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 08:21 Jared Lowe wrote:
> > Thanks Aditya/Marissa — quick clarity from our side.
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: BrightHealth MAP pressure — request for short extension + credit approval (if needed)

Thanks for the clear summary. Approved with conditions. Executive decision: we will authorize Path A (provisional appendix + conditional 10% credit) under these constraints: 

1) Credit cap: credit limited to one invoice cycle / max $15k.
2) MAP update: Aditya to update MAP doc with Path A dates and stamp the acceptance path; Marissa to publish an updated risk log and owner matrix.
3) Legal & Finance: Legal to issue provisional appendix template within 24 hours; Finance to prepare a credit memo template (cc: finance@redwood.ai).
4) Customer comms: Aditya to send a single message to BrightHealth confirming the provisional path and the conditional credit terms; copy Legal and Finance.

Marissa / Aditya — please complete the MAP update and send the external comms today. Once Legal posts the appendix, I'll confirm the exec note in writing.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
